citations.text:
Card Dispute Procedure
2. Intake and Timeframes

Members must report an unauthorized or disputed card transaction within 60 days of the statement date on which the transaction first appeared. Disputes received after this period are still logged, but Harbor's liability protections and the member's right to provisional credit may be limited.

For every dispute, the agent completes Form HCU-DSP-114 (Card Transaction Dispute) during the initial contact, whether the contact is by phone, in branch, or through secure message. The form captures the transaction date, amount, merchant descriptor, the member's explanation, and whether the card is still in the member's possession.

1. Verify the caller using the standard three-factor authentication script.

2. Confirm the transaction details against the card processing system.

3. If fraud is suspected, block the card immediately and order a replacement.

4. Complete Form HCU-DSP-114 and read the dispute acknowledgment disclosure.

5. Route the case to the Card Services dispute queue in the case management system.
citations.title: Card Dispute Procedure

answer: For a domestic wire to another bank, send your request by 3:00 p.m. Eastern Time on a business day and it will be processed that same day, under the Wire Transfer Policy (Rev 2026-02). Requests received after 3:00 p.m., or on a non-business day, go out the next business day. If it's an international wire, the cutoff is earlier — 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time — for same-day release.

citations.text:
5. Processing Cutoff Times

Domestic wire requests received and verified by 3:00 p.m. Eastern Time on a business day are processed the same business day. Requests received after the cutoff, or on a day that is not a business day, are processed on the next business day. International wire requests must be received and verified by 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time to be released the same business day; delivery to the beneficiary may take one to five business days depending on the destination country and intermediary banks.
citations.title: Wire Transfer Policy

Separately, if an Overdraft Transfer Protection transfer from a linked Primary Share Account is used, only one $5.00 transfer fee is charged per business day, regardless of how many items it covers. citations.text:
Harbor Credit Union Overdraft Policy
4. Overdraft Fees

Harbor charges a fee of $29 per item, up to a maximum of three (3) items per business day, for items paid through Courtesy Pay. No overdraft fee will be charged if the account is overdrawn by $25.00 or less at the end of the business day, and no fee is charged for items that Harbor returns unpaid under this policy. Returned item (NSF) fees are listed in the Schedule of Fees and Charges.

Overdraft Transfer Protection transfers from a linked Primary Share Account carry a transfer fee of $5.00 per transfer. Only one transfer fee is assessed per business day regardless of how many items the transfer covers.
